parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no traveler-facing restriction: no entry screening, facility ban, care denial, criminalisation of expression, or trans-specific violence figure. Same-sex conduct is legal and regional courts function for trans people (2024 AG opinion, March 2025 rectification ruling, April 2026 Article 2 finding). The gender-recognition ban and adoption/marriage bars are resident-facing climate signals, not visitor exposures. Weighing down: documented official hostility (smear campaigns, 'destructive gender ideologies'), scapegoating found discriminatory in 2026, hostile laws still in force, and a Pride-harassment history — tier-3 societal hostility, but with operative supranational recourse. The April 2026 election and Court ruling signal shift; repeal pace is unresolved. Detention conditions for LGBTIQ people are reported (2025) but content unstated.

entry_documents.exposure: Visitor carries home passport; jurisdiction records birth marker, but no documented entry screening or pat-down practice for trans travelers (explicitly not counted). Mismatch risk derives from the traveler's own papers.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border friction, marker scrutiny, or document-mismatch procedure at ports of entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Documentation rules interact with everyday bureaucracy only for residents; no path from entry to detention documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A 2025 national report documents LGBTIQ detainees' situation and rights in national detention facilities amid the hostile legal climate; contents unstated, so severity unknown.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Regional court jurisdiction, habeas-type remedies and an EU-funded detainees' rights project imply oversight infrastructure.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest for unrelated conduct would place a trans visitor in this documented detention setting.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access (bathroom/ward) rule for visitors is documented; no subnational variation exists in the record.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented facility exclusion applying to trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Legal architecture is national; nothing local layers onto it.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial, HRT seizure, or ward misplacement for visitors; the 2021 child-protection law's under-18 gender-change ban is resident-facing.
care_services.protection: Regional Court's April 2026 ruling found the child-protection law discriminatory; rectification jurisprudence shows courts working for trans people.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor seeking care interacts with an in-force ban not yet shown repealed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented state threat-framing under prior government: PM's 'gays leave children alone,' 'destructive gender ideologies' resolution, government-linked pedophilia smears; April 2026 Court found scapegoating. Laws remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Government changed April 2026; Court of Justice Article 2 breach finding; Pride draws tens of thousands; repeal pledges on adoption.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing shapes police/social encounters, but supranational courts constrain enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 gender-change ban (child-protection law) is in force; constitution bars same-sex adoption. Resident-facing; no documented application to a visiting trans minor or guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: April 2026 ruling found the law discriminatory; repeal trajectory unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure is open, not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans homicide or violence figures provided; background-rate test cannot apply. Dated 2014 far-right Pride abuse and smear campaigns evidence social hostility framing (tier 3), not violence patterns.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Large 2026 Pride; same-sex activity legal since 1961; functioning courts.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assembly hostility is the documented street-facing exposure for visible attendees.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Repeal pace unresolved; new party silent on LGBTQ rights; hostile architecture still operative; appeal status of 2022 ruling unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Regional Court rectification ruling (2025) is operative authority; April 2026 Article 2 finding; constitutional and supreme courts active; election ended 16-year rule.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Supranational remedies offset national hostility where they reach the traveler.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and registers transgender visitors with routine refusal. Here no entry restriction, register, or reporting duty for trans visitors is documented at all; worst documented feature is official/social hostility with working supranational courts — materially safer.

Kestrel Isles has discretionary secondary screening and variable entry refusals with slow appeals. This dossier documents no screening conduct whatsoever and shows courts actually ruling for trans people, so it sits above 0.55 despite hostile national laws.

Meridia trains border officers, recognises markers, and offers tribunal compensation. Here no border protections, training, or visitor-specific remedy are documented and hostile laws remain in force — one step below, since documented state hostility outranks unstated procedures.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a resident-facing hostile architecture (2020 gender-recognition ban, marriage/adoption constitutional bars, child-protection law) layered under functioning supranational courts that have ruled for trans people and against the state's founding-values compliance. For a visitor the operative exposure is documentation mismatch plus documented official and social hostility framing — not criminalisation, not a documented border procedure, not documented violence. The April 2026 election and Article 2 finding shift climate but repeal is unresolved, so hostile laws count as in force while mitigation counts only where shown operating. Net: elevated friction and outing potential with real but unguaranteed remedies, no custody pathway documented.
